reasoning: The defect is fixed. UpdateChecker.swift:125-127 (isCheckDue) says a check is due when there is no previous check, when the last check was on an earlier local calendar day (calendar.isDate(_:inSameDayAs:)), or when 24 h or more have passed. A last check in the future is never due (the lastCheck <= now guard). UpdateChecker.swift:133-143 (delayUntilNextCheck) returns 0 when a check is due. Otherwise it returns min(end of lastCheck's local day, lastCheck+24h) - now, clamped to 60 s...86400 s. The checkIfNeeded gate at :176 uses the same predicate, so no second path still applies the old 24 h rule. The loop at RefreshScheduler.swift:187-201 checks at launch, then recomputes the delay from the stored last-check date on every round. It keeps [weak self] (it breaks when self is gone), the Task.isCancelled checks before and after the sleep, and the config.enabled and status.isBusy gates inside checkIfNeeded. recordCheckDate runs before the fetch (UpdateChecker.swift:193), so a network failure does not cause a 60 s retry loop. The production sleeper is still Task.sleep(for:), which uses ContinuousClock, so an overnight system sleep counts toward the midnight wake-up. The tests are deterministic: a fixed Gregorian calendar in America/Sao_Paulo, an injected now, a ScriptedSleeper with no real sleep, a URLProtocol stub that fails or hangs so no network is reached, and a suite-named UserDefaults. The DST cases check out. On 2018-11-04 the day starts at 01:00, so 22:00 -> 23:00 on 11-03 gives a 3600 s delay. On 2019-02-16 the day is 25 h long, so the 24 h bound wins at 23 h, and a check 24 h later on the same local day is due. The relaunch case is covered: 23:34 -> 10:00 the next day checks at launch (RefreshSchedulerTests:344, status .checking), then sleeps 14 h until midnight. I ran the filter UpdateCheckDueTests|RefreshSchedulerTests: 22/22 green. For the reversal I kept the new API so the tests still compile, restored the old behaviour in the code (a 24 h-only predicate, delay = 86400, loop sleep 86400) and re-ran: RED with 12 issues in 8 tests, including the relaunch, same_day, previous_day, both DST-start cases, dst_end_uses_24h_bound, floor and checkIfNeeded tests. I then restored both files, and the working-tree diff is byte-identical to reviews/diffs/B17-update-sched.diff (cmp). On the unrequested change (RefreshScheduler.swift:187, the loop never starts when enabled=false): this is not a regression. UpdateChecker.config is a `let` (UpdateChecker.swift:68). The single UpdateChecker is built once in AiTaskbarApp.swift:21 from env.config.updates, and a Settings save only raises the 'relaunch to apply' banner (SettingsViewModel.swift:8-9). Before the fix, a loop running with enabled=false would have woken daily and checkIfNeeded would have returned at the enabled guard every time. Turning updates on at runtime therefore never took effect before, and cannot now, without a relaunch. After a relaunch, start() evaluates the new config.
